messages:
Anna L.: Quick design review request — thinking about moving the legend into a compact chip/group area at the top-right to save vertical space, and adding a visual 'spike-cap' to indicate outlier clamping instead of full-scale spikes. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/compact-legend-spike-cap ; want feedback on copy + a11y concerns.

Mike R.: Love the compact legend for dashboards with many series. Question: do chips show the current series color + inline unit? e.g., "rps" or "ms"?

Anna L.: Yes — chips would show color swatch + short unit label. For series where units differ we propose a unit-toggle at the top of the chart (global per-widget) rather than per-chip. Keeps chips compact.

Keiko H.: Concern: if we rely on color + tiny label, color-only won't pass WCAG for low-vision users. We should add a keyboard-focusable region for each chip and aria-label like "Series: request latency, unit: ms, visible". Also ensure the unit toggle is reachable via keyboard.

Mike R.: Agreed on aria. Also: how does the spike-cap work? Is it visual only or does it change the y-axis scale?

Anna L.: Proposal: spike-cap is a soft clamp — long-tail points beyond X percentile are rendered as capped markers (little capped-top icon) and we show a tooltip summary: "N points capped at > 95th pct (value shown)". The y-axis still reflects full range but we add a faint ghost region to indicate truncated values. The intent is to avoid single spikes from dominating perceived trends.

Sara (PM): Quick product ask — can the cap threshold be user-editable (preset choices: 99th/95th/auto)? Also need a clear legend entry explaining what capped means — users were confused in last test.

Anna L.: Yes presets + an "auto" that picks percentile based on series variance. For legend copy: proposing short help text inline: "Spikes capped: high outliers shown as ••• (click to expand)". Open to wording suggestions.

Keiko H.: Copy nit: avoid "capped" since it sounds destructive. Maybe "condensed" or "summarized". Example: "High outliers condensed — click to expand". Also ensure screen readers announce when points are condensed.

Mike R.: UI nit: when multiple series are condensed simultaneously, we need a combined control to expand all. Maybe a small pull-down in the unit-toggle area: "Show condensed spikes" with per-series expand options.

Anna L.: Good call. Design update: small caret next to unit-toggle opens a menu with "Expand condensed spikes (global)" + per-series toggles.

design-bot: Checklist: 1) keyboard focus for chips ✅ 2) aria-labels for chips ✅ 3) unit-toggle keyboard reachable ✅ 4) spike-cap icon + tooltip design ✅ 5) additive combined expand control TODO 6) user-friendly copy iteration TODO

Sara (PM): Two quick asks before we ship: (1) run a short usability test with 5 users to validate copy and discoverability; (2) add an analytics event when users expand condensed spikes so we can measure usage.

Anna L.: Sounds good. I'll iterate copy (using "condensed"), tweak the figma, and hand off accessibility notes. Will drop updated link in this thread when ready. Thanks for the quick reviews :thumbsup:

Keiko H.: Thanks — ping me for the a11y review once updated.

Mike R.: Also, for the backend: we need a flag in the timeseries pipeline to emit "condensed_count" and a sample of top values for tooltip. @infra for FYI when this moves to implementation.

Anna L.: noted — I'll add the data contract to the spec doc. End of thread for now.
